title: HIGH-DOSE TARGETED RADIATION FOLLOWED BY CHEMOIMMUNOTHERAPY FOR ADVANCED BILE-DUCT CANCER IN HOUSTON'S SAFETY-NET POPULATION
official: THE HOPE-CCA PILOT: HIGH-DOSE TARGETED RADIATION FOLLOWED BY CHEMOIMMUNOTHERAPY FOR ADVANCED BILE-DUCT CANCER IN HOUSTON'S SAFETY-NET POPULATION
summary:
The purpose of this study is to learn whether a treatment sequence of high-dose radiation followed by chemotherapy and immunotherapy can be delivered safely and on schedule to patients with bile duct cancer (cholangiocarcinoma) inside the liver that cannot be removed with surgery.

Participants first receive targeted, high-dose radiation therapy to the liver tumor over 15 treatments (about 3 weeks), with capecitabine, an oral chemotherapy pill taken on radiation days to make the radiation more effective. After a 4 to 6 week recovery and restaging period, participants receive the standard combination of durvalumab (an immunotherapy), gemcitabine, and cisplatin for up to 8 cycles, followed by durvalumab alone as maintenance. All treatments are FDA-approved and used as standard care; the study evaluates the order in which they are given.

The main question is whether at least 9 of 12 participants can complete radiation and start chemoimmunotherapy within 8 weeks. The study also tracks side effects, tumor control, survival, quality of life, and barriers to care. It is enrolling at Harris Health System and Baylor St. Luke's Medical Center in Houston, Texas.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 18 years or older
* Histologically or cytologically confirmed intrahepatic or perihilar cholangiocarcinoma
* Locally advanced, unresectable disease as determined by multidisciplinary tumor board review including a hepatobiliary surgeon
* Regional or non-regional nodal metastases permitted if all involved nodes can be safely encompassed within the radiation field; no other distant metastases
* Not a candidate for liver transplantation
* Measurable or evaluable disease on contrast-enhanced CT or MRI
* No prior liver radiation; no prior systemic therapy for cholangiocarcinoma, except one cycle of gemcitabine and cisplatin, with or without durvalumab, before registration
* ECOG performance status 0 to 2
* Child-Pugh class A or B7
* Tumor anatomy permitting safe delivery of 67.5 Gy in 15 fractions, with uninvolved liver volume of at least 700 mL
* Adequate biliary drainage if biliary obstruction was present, with total bilirubin no more than 3 times the upper limit of normal
* Adequate bone marrow, liver, and kidney function, including creatinine clearance of at least 50 mL/min
* Negative pregnancy test for those of childbearing potential, and agreement to use effective contraception during treatment and for 14 months after the last dose
* Medical coverage for standard-of-care therapy (Harris Health financial assistance, Medicaid, Medicare, or commercial insurance); study staff will help uninsured patients apply for financial assistance
* Able to understand and sign informed consent in English or Spanish

Exclusion Criteria:

* Distant metastases (peritoneal, lung, bone, or other visceral sites) or nodal disease that cannot be safely included in the radiation field
* Gallbladder cancer, ampullary cancer, or distal extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
* Child-Pugh class B8 or worse, clinically significant ascites, or overt hepatic encephalopathy within 6 months
* Prior upper abdominal radiation that would overlap the planned treatment field
* Prior anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, or anti-CTLA-4 therapy, other than durvalumab given in the single permitted pre-registration cycle
* Active or uncontrolled infection, including cholangitis or liver abscess, within 14 days
* Autoimmune disease requiring systemic treatment within the past 2 years (vitiligo, alopecia, hypothyroidism on stable replacement, and psoriasis not requiring systemic therapy are permitted)
* Need for chronic systemic immunosuppression, including prednisone above 10 mg/day or equivalent, that cannot be tapered before chemoimmunotherapy
* Prior organ or allogeneic stem cell transplant
* History of interstitial lung disease or non-infectious pneumonitis requiring steroids
* Active hepatitis B or C unless on suppressive or curative antiviral therapy; HIV permitted if CD4 count is at least 200/uL with undetectable viral load on therapy
* Untreated varices with bleeding or high bleeding risk, or gastrointestinal bleeding within 3 months
* Grade 2 or higher peripheral neuropathy or clinically significant hearing loss precluding cisplatin
* Known complete DPD deficiency
* Clinically significant cardiovascular disease, including NYHA class III to IV heart failure, myocardial infarction, or unstable angina within 6 months
* Another active malignancy requiring treatment within the past 2 years, except adequately treated non-melanoma skin cancer, carcinoma in situ, or low-risk prostate cancer under active surveillance
* Known hypersensitivity to durvalumab, gemcitabine, cisplatin, or capecitabine
* Pregnant or breastfeeding
* Concurrent participation in another interventional therapeutic trial
* Incarcerated or detained at the time of enrollment
* Psychiatric illness or social situation that would preclude safe completion of therapy or informed consent
